title: Atomoxetine attenuates methotrexate-induced lung injury in rats implicating TLR4/NF-kappaB and Bax/Bcl-2/caspase-3 signaling cascades: a study based on molecular docking and experimental validation.
authors: Mohyeldin, Reham H; Sharata, Ehab E; Ibrahim, Ayman M; Attya, Mina Ezzat; Kotb, Al Shaimaa Mahmoud; Rofaeil, Remon Roshdy; Khalifa, Yassmen Mohamed Montaser A; Abdelnaser, Mahmoud
one_liner_zh: 该研究为动物实验探究药物对肺损伤的保护作用，仅涉及分子对接作为辅助手段，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Methotrexate (MTX) is frequently used to treat a variety of autoimmune diseases and malignancies, but its use is restricted due to a number of side effects, including lung damage. For the first time, this study attempts to assess the potential protective advantages of atomoxetine (ATOM) against MTX-induced lung damage in rats. MTX was used to cause lung damage. A total of 24 male Wistar albino rats were used in this study. Animals were randomly allocated to four experimental groups of six rats each: (Ⅰ) Control group, (Ⅱ) ATOM group, (Ⅲ) MTX group, and (Ⅳ) MTX+ATOM group. Malondialdehyde (MDA), glutathione (GSH), and superoxide dismutase (SOD) levels in the lungs were measured. ELISA was used to measure the levels of lung IL-10, interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-alpha), Bcl-2-associated X protein (Bax), and B-cell lymphoma 2 (Bcl-2). NF-kappaB p65 and caspase-3 were evaluated using immunohistochemistry. Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) and myeloid differentiation primary response 88 (MYD88) protein expression levels were assessed using the Western blot technique. A histopathological study of lung tissues was performed. Lung MDA, IL-6, TNF-alpha, and Bax levels were significantly increased by MTX, while GSH, SOD, IL-10, and Bcl-2 levels were significantly decreased. Additionally, this led to the overexpression of the proteins TLR4 and MYD88. Additionally, the MTX group had higher immunopositivity for both NF-kappaB p65 and caspase-3. All of the aforementioned biochemical and histological abnormalities were greatly improved with ATOM. ATOM significantly improved MTX-induced pulmonary injury by suppressing TLR4/MYD88/NF-kappaB p65 and caspase-3-mediated apoptotic signaling pathways.
abstract_zh: 甲氨蝶呤（Methotrexate, MTX）常用于治疗多种自身免疫性疾病和恶性肿瘤，但其使用因多种副作用（包括肺损伤）而受到限制。本研究首次尝试评估托莫西汀（atomoxetine, ATOM）对大鼠MTX诱导肺损伤的潜在保护作用。采用MTX诱导肺损伤。本研究共使用24只雄性Wistar白化大鼠。动物随机分为四个实验组，每组6只：（Ⅰ）对照组，（Ⅱ）ATOM组，（Ⅲ）MTX组，（Ⅳ）MTX+ATOM组。测定肺组织中丙二醛（MDA）、谷胱甘肽（GSH）和超氧化物歧化酶（SOD）水平。采用ELISA法测定肺组织白细胞介素-10（IL-10）、白细胞介素-6（interleukin-6, IL-6）、肿瘤坏死因子-α（tumor necrosis factor-alpha, TNF-alpha）、Bcl-2相关X蛋白（Bax）和B细胞淋巴瘤2（Bcl-2）水平。采用免疫组织化学法评估NF-kappaB p65和caspase-3。采用Western blot技术评估Toll样受体4（Toll-like receptor 4, TLR4）和髓样分化初级反应蛋白88（myeloid differentiation primary response 88, MYD88）蛋白表达水平。对肺组织进行组织病理学研究。MTX显著增加肺组织MDA、IL-6、TNF-alpha和Bax水平，同时显著降低GSH、SOD、IL-10和Bcl-2水平。此外，这导致TLR4和MYD88蛋白过表达。同时，MTX组NF-kappaB p65和caspase-3的免疫阳性率均升高。ATOM显著改善上述所有生化和组织学异常。ATOM通过抑制TLR4/MYD88/NF-kappaB p65和caspase-3介导的凋亡信号通路，显著改善MTX诱导的肺损伤。
